prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
I don’t have live web access to look up current local businesses, but I can help you find a qualified backflow tester/repairer near Liberty, MO and tell you what to check for. Do you want residential or commercial service? Meanwhile, here’s a practical plan and everything to ask:

Where to look
- City of Liberty Water Department or Public Works — they often keep a list of approved/certified testers or have rules on who can submit test results.
- Google Maps, Yelp, Nextdoor, Angi/HomeAdvisor — search terms: “backflow testing Liberty MO”, “backflow tester near me”, “cross-connection control tester”.
- Local plumbing companies, irrigation companies, and fire-protection contractors — many offer backflow testing/repair.

Credentials and things to verify
- Tester certification: look for a recognized backflow tester certification (often called backflow assembly tester, cross-connection control tester). Common standards include ASSE 5110 or state/utility-accepted certifications. Ask which cert they hold.
- Proof the test gauge used is calibrated within the last 12 months.
- Insurance — general liability and workers’ comp.
- Experience with your type of device (residential irrigation, commercial double-check, reduced pressure principle device, fire-line assemblies).
- References or reviews from other Liberty/Kansas City area customers.

Questions to ask a company
- Are you certified to test backflow assemblies? Which certification do you hold?
- Do you calibrate your test gauges annually? Can you show calibration proof?
- Will you provide the required test report form and submit it to the City (if necessary)?
- Do you handle both testing and on-site repairs? What are your repair rates?
- Do you charge a travel fee or a separate fee for failing tests/repairs?

Typical costs (ballpark)
- Testing only: roughly $50–$150 per device (depends on type and area).
- Repairs: can range from small part swaps ($50–$200+) to major rebuilds or replacement ($300–$1,500+), depending on the device and parts/labor.

What to expect during an appointment
- The tester locates the assembly, attaches a test gauge, performs the required checks, and records results.
- If it fails, they should explain the defect and give a repair estimate or perform repairs if authorized.
- After testing they should provide a written test report and (if required) submit results to the City of Liberty or your water provider.

If you’d like, I can:
- Draft a phone script or email you can use to contact local companies.
- Give an exact Google search string and filters to find nearby testers.
- If you paste a few business names/links you found, I can help evaluate them.

Which would you prefer?
